ian.forIanText: Skip to content GTM People ← Back to the concept JUST FOR YOUR EYES · OCTOBER 2026 For Ian — what changed and why. The page at this address is a concept on our own domain. Nothing touches gtm-people.com. Every fact on it — the specialisms, the six-step process, the TaaS tiers and fee rules, the 2026 salary bands, the eight FAQs, the 28 partners and the 25 open roles — comes from your live site and its public roles feed, copied verbatim. I invented no quotes, prices, testimonials or article titles. The design goal was measurable: the same story, with far less on screen at any one moment. Your home page is one long scroll of fifteen different layouts. The concept tells it as a scroll-story — one idea per screen, with pinned sections that swap their content in place as you scroll — so the reader never meets a wall of text, yet nothing is cut. Two cuts / is the scroll-story: one idea per screen; the hero, the specialisms and the open roles are pinned and change under your thumb. /deck/ is the compact tabbed cut: two desktop screens, ten tabs, every panel one tap away. Both carry the same copy. Tell me which direction you'd back and I'll take that one to a finished build. Today / Concept MEASURE TODAY (GTM-PEOPLE.COM) CONCEPT (SCROLL-STORY · DECK) Distinct section layouts 15 13 (14 sections; the card stack is used twice) · 10 panels in one layout Words visible per screen, desktop (median · max, sampled every 400 px) 190 · 392 35 · 295 Words of your copy carried over 4,373 on the page 3,410 — every sentence of the site copy; the 25 roles shown as title, location, stage and comp (descriptions stay disclosed at shortlist) · deck 5,005 incl. descriptions Third-party scripts 3 (Google Tag Manager, Supabase CDN, Cloudflare Insights) 0 · one host for fonts Largest text wall (tallest run of consecutive paragraphs, desktop) 420 px — the About block 348 px — the same About block, kept word for word Scrolling to reach pricing via the menu No menu link — 9.6 screens desktop, 20.3 mobile 0 — "Pricing" in the header on both cuts Page weight (first load, desktop) 1,004 KB · 41 requests 152 KB · 7 requests (89 KB of that is the page itself) · deck 132 KB Page height, desktop / mobile 17,828 px / 36,490 px 52,167 px / 27,515 px — on purpose: pinned sections turn scroll into a controller, so height is track length, not reading length · deck 1,773 / 2,941 px Measured 2026-10-06 with Playwright at 1440×900 and 390×844, default state, after the fonts loaded. Numbers are in research

ian.founderText: “Revenue is a hiring problem. We fix it.” — Ian Harwood, Founder ABOUT GTM PEOPLE Built by someone who's been in the seat. GTM People was founded by Ian Harwood — a specialist GTM recruiter with over 20 years of experience placing sales, marketing, RevOps, and CS leaders across the UK and Europe. After over two decades placing GTM talent — first at generalist agencies, then building a specialist SaaS-focused recruitment desk — Ian saw the same problem repeated with every early-stage client: they were getting a generalist recruitment process applied to a highly specialist hiring challenge. Early-stage SaaS hiring is different. The profile that succeeds at a 30-person Series A looks nothing like the person who thrives at a 300-person Series C. The motivation, the risk appetite, the skills that matter — completely different. Most recruiters don't know the difference. We do, because we've sp
ian.taasText: WHY TAAS? Traditional recruitment has the wrong incentives. A traditional agency gets paid once — when you make the hire. That means their interest ends the moment the contract is signed. TaaS flips the model. TRADITIONAL AGENCY GTM PEOPLE TAAS Per-hire fee creates pressure to fill fast, not well Monthly retainer means we care about long-term quality No incentive to care what happens after placement Your talent partner stays embedded in your team Candidates often oversold to get the fee Candidates are briefed fully — no surprises after joining Every search starts from scratch Pipeline always warm — next hire is faster than the last You're a transaction, not a relationship 3-month guarantee on every placement
